correctness.rationale: For exactly 256 labeled four-base words, reverse complementation has 16 fixed words and 120 nonfixed two-word orbits; all 120 two-word orbits are internally single-deletion compatible. Their finite compatibility graph has edges precisely when full deletion shadows are disjoint, establishing a code/clique bijection. The packaged C++17 recurrence exhaustively certifies 0 twelve-orbit cliques and exactly 44 eleven-orbit cliques with safe greedy-coloring upper-bound pruning, using no optimization heuristic. A genuinely separate standard-library Python Bron-Kerbosch maximal-clique enumeration reproduces the 44 complete lists, excludes larger maximal cliques, checks nine group orbits (seven size four, two size eight), and intersects codebooks to identify exactly two compulsory reverse-complement pairs. The actual packaged sources and data were compiled/executed and cross-checked. No infinite extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: The exact maximum size 22 for this very same model is expressly credited to D'yachkov et al. (2005), Example 5 and Remark 4, and is not counted as a discovery. Their inspected text gives a single size-22 construction and asserts optimality, but not the complete number 44 of labeled optima, their nine equivalence classes, or the two compulsory pairs. Historical searches and closest available published records did not supply the latter characterization; a one-page 2006 remark remains inaccessible and is a named priority risk.
residual_risks: The full one-page 2006 remark to the same-model 2005 paper was inaccessible; its precise content could affect historical-priority comparison.
Search-index coverage of older tables and unpublished collections is not complete; numerical nonappearance is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: At the first small quaternary case explicitly treated in the original DNA deletion-code literature, prior work establishes the maximum code size but leaves the full optimal design space undescribed. The finite classification determines all 44 labeled maximum codebooks, their nine symmetry types, and two unavoidable homopolymer pairs, resolving a natural structurally motivated question relevant to selecting additional constraints on optimal designs. It is not an arbitrary parameter substitution or a routine increment of a previous enumeration: it classifies the complete extremal family of a published exact model. No thermodynamic advantage is claimed.
